title: Introduce semantic-stratifier and prioritized-degradation-pinger CI hook
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: We see noisy regression alerts when prompt-set failures affect low-impact cohorts. This PR introduces two cooperating components: 1) a semantic-stratifier sampler that tags evaluation requests with a semantic-impact bucket (high/medium/low) based on prompt set metadata and a lightweight embedding similarity heuristic, and 2) a prioritized-degradation-pinger CI hook that surfaces regressions with an impact-aware severity and can suppress or delay low-impact noisy alerts.

Summary of changes: implemented a new stratifier in eval_harness/samplers that computes cohort-level semantic density and assigns priority scores, added a CI hook that consumes eval run summaries and escalates only when degradation score crosses tiered thresholds, and wired the hook into our CI decision flow. The hook supports a soft-fail mode that records failure telemetry but prevents blocking merges for low-impact regressions.

Behavioral notes and backward compatibility: default configuration preserves current gating behavior (no suppression). The new stratifier is opt-in via the eval config (enable_semantic_stratifier: true). When enabled, the hook augments existing regression reports with impact tags but does not change existing hard-fail thresholds unless the repo enables the prioritized policy.

Testing and validation: unit tests for stratifier heuristics and CI hook logic were added; integration smoke test included a replay of two historical failing runs (one high-impact, one low-impact) to validate scoring and suppress behavior. Performance: sampling and tagging adds ~12ms median overhead per sample in the local runner; no measurable CI pipeline slowdowns observed in stage.

How to enable: add enable_semantic_stratifier: true under eval_runs in your repo's ci-eval.yml and set degrade_policy: prioritized in ci/hooks.yaml. Example config snippets are in docs/ci_hooks.md.

Rollback: disable the flag or flip degrade_policy to legacy in ci/hooks.yaml; a backfill tool is included to re-evaluate recent alerts if teams choose to reclassify events.

Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration replay smoke test - [x] docs updated - [x] changelog entry - [x] feature flagged and opt-in

Related: ENG-1932 (prioritization epic), infra/observability ticket PM-411 for alert UX follow-up.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice approach; can you add a short note on the embedding model you used and rationale for the 0.72 similarity cutoff?
Asha Patel: Added a comment in semantic_stratifier.py and included a unit test covering the 0.72 threshold rationale; also documented rationale in docs/ci_hooks.md.
Ellen Cho: The soft-fail path looks good, but we need metrics to ensure we don't accidentally suppress systemic regressions. Add a prometheus counter for suppressed_high_impact_alerts.

Asha Patel: Added prometheus counters and an alert in ci/hooks/register_hooks.py that fires if suppressed_high_impact_alerts > 0 for 5m in stage. Updated tests to assert counter increments when suppression would have occurred.
Priya Nair: Approving pending a small nit: prefer a clearer variable name than `sd_score` in the scorer utils.
Asha Patel: Renamed sd_score to semantic_density_score across files and updated tests. Thank you!
tests_run_summary: Unit suite: 72 tests, 0 failures; Integration replay: 2 historical runs validated; Perf microbench: median +12ms/sample overhead; Prometheus counters exercised in stage.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in semantic stratifier sampler and an impact-aware CI hook that reduces noisy low-impact regression alerts while preserving hard-fail protections for high-impact regressions. Feature is opt-in and configurable via ci hooks.
notes_for_oncall: If teams enable prioritized policy and unexpectedly stop seeing alerts, verify: (1) ci/hooks.yaml degrade_policy is not set to prioritized, (2) prometheus suppressed_high_impact_alerts counter is zero; backfill tool can reclassify alerts if needed.
safety_considerations: No model weights or PII introduced. Embedding calls are cached and rate-limited; default stratifier uses a small CPU-only embedding fallback when external vector service is unavailable.
